evals.prompt: We need a full penetration test of our company's external infrastructure. We're a mid-sized SaaS company running a customer-facing web app at app.example.com, an API at api.example.com, and a VPN gateway for remote employees. Our internal IP range is 203.0.113.0/24. We've authorized testing of all external-facing systems but explicitly exclude production databases and the internal HR portal. We need a complete assessment with a report for our board. Where do we start?
evals.expected_output: Classify this as a Web2 pentest engagement. Start with Phase 1: Reconnaissance using recon — enumerate subdomains, fingerprint services on app.example.com and api.example.com, scan the external IP range 203.0.113.0/24, and identify the VPN gateway. Then proceed through the standard pipeline: Phase 2 Security Audit (audit) for code review, configuration audit, and OWASP Top 10 testing; Phase 3 Exploitation (exploit) to validate findings with controlled attacks; Phase 4 Verification (verify) to filter false positives; and Phase 6 Reporting (report) to deliver a board-ready pentest report. Note that production databases and the internal HR portal are out of scope — document this scope boundary in the engagement log. Use CVSS v3.1 severity ratings. Maintain an engagement tracker throughout.

evals.prompt: I'm the CTO of a DeFi startup. We're about to launch a lending protocol on Ethereum mainnet next month and need a smart contract audit before we go live. The protocol has a lending pool contract, an oracle integration for price feeds, and a governance token. We've had the code internally reviewed but want an external audit. TVL is expected to be around $50M at launch. We need to know if there are any critical vulnerabilities before we deploy.
evals.expected_output: Classify this as a Web3 audit engagement. Start with Phase 1: Reconnaissance using recon — identify the chain (Ethereum mainnet), profile the contract addresses, verify contract source code on Etherscan, and map the protocol architecture (lending pool, oracle integration, governance token). Then proceed through: Phase 2 Security Audit (audit) for contract audit, protocol economic security analysis, formal verification of critical invariants, and known vulnerability pattern matching (reentrancy, oracle manipulation, access control); Phase 3 Exploitation (exploit) to validate any findings through controlled contract exploitation including flash loan attack simulations and oracle manipulation; Phase 4 Verification (verify) to confirm findings with deterministic reproduction; and Phase 6 Reporting (report) to deliver an audit report. Use Immunefi severity scale — with $50M TVL, any fund loss vulnerability is Critical. Note that the governance token and oracle integration are in scope. Maintain an engagement tracker throughout.

evals.prompt: We're a crypto exchange and need a comprehensive security assessment. Our platform consists of: (1) a React frontend at trade.example.com, (2) a Node.js trading API at api.example.com, (3) a set of smart contracts on Ethereum for custody and settlement, and (4) AWS infrastructure hosting everything. We've authorized testing of all components. We've had a minor security incident in the past and want to make sure we're not vulnerable to a repeat. We need a full assessment covering everything — frontend, API, contracts, and infrastructure.
evals.expected_output: Classify this as a Mixed engagement (web3 protocol with web2 components). Start with Phase 1: Reconnaissance using recon — enumerate the full attack surface across all four components: the React frontend (trade.example.com), the Node.js trading API (api.example.com), the Ethereum smart contracts (custody and settlement), and the AWS infrastructure. Map how these components interact. Then proceed through: Phase 2 Security Audit (audit) covering both web2 (frontend code review, API security, AWS configuration audit, OWASP Top 10) and web3 (contract audit, protocol economic security, custody contract analysis); Phase 3 Exploitation (exploit) to validate findings across both domains — web exploitation for frontend/API, contract exploitation for smart contracts; Phase 4 Verification (verify) to filter false positives across all components; and Phase 6 Reporting (report) to deliver a unified report. Use CVSS v3.1 for web2 findings and Immunefi scale for web3 findings. Given the past incident, consider whether a forensics review of the previous incident should be included. Maintain an engagement tracker throughout.
